fields.Front: Give three advantages of a DBMS over a flat file system.
fields.Back: Any three of: reduced data redundancy/inconsistency; isolates programs from the data; persistent storage between program runs; multiple users can share the data; more abstract conceptual views; security, integrity and backups; generalized query tools; multiple user interfaces; enforced standards (centralized data); reduced development time; up-to-date information managed centrally.

fields.Front: What are the three disadvantages of a DBMS compared with flat files (from the lecture notes)?
fields.Back: Cost (flat files are free; note MySQL and PostgreSQL are also free now, but some DBMSs are very expensive), initial complexity (you must build a model and tables first), and the need for trained/skilled staff to maintain it.

fields.Text: Three disadvantages of a DBMS: {{c1::cost}}, {{c2::initial complexity}}, and the need for {{c3::skilled/trained people}}.

fields.Front: Which DBMS advantage means programs no longer need to know the byte layout of the data?
fields.Back: Isolation of programs from the data (program-data independence).

fields.Text: The DBMS advantage that lets you ask new questions without writing a new program is {{c1::generalized query tools (a query language)}}.
Orders flat file: one address was entered as 'Oxford Street West' and the next as 'Richmond St' with 'W', so the data became {{c1::inconsistent}}; a DBMS reduces {{c2::redundancy and inconsistency}}.

fields.Front: Orders flat file: the price $76 was an integer, then a later record stored $76.00 as a real. What problem does the instructor say this illustrates?
fields.Back: The reading code has to change, so the code is no longer isolated/abstracted from the data (program-data dependence). A DBMS isolates programs from the data.

fields.Text: Instructor on persistence: with a DBMS, if a program {{c1::crashes in the middle of a write}}, we know we are not going to lose any data.

fields.Front: What is the instructor's example of a DBMS providing 'multiple user interfaces'?
fields.Back: One MySQL database accessed online through JavaScript or PHP by one person, and through plain Java or Python code by another.

fields.Text: Cost is a smaller DBMS disadvantage today because {{c1::MySQL and PostgreSQL}} are free, although some DBMSs (e.g. commercial ones) can be {{c2::very expensive}}.
'Initially it's very complex': before you can store anything in a DBMS you must {{c1::come up with a model}} and then {{c2::build the tables}}.

fields.Front: What is the instructor's example of DBMS security?
fields.Back: Not just anyone can use the database; users must have a user ID.
